title: Gabrd knockdown produces a narrow thalamic Cttnbp2-positive delta-GABA-A response
exact_observed_result: Gabrd knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c had strong target depletion and exactly one FDR<0.05 non-target row, Cttnbp2 up. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Gabrd was also FDR-depleted but produced no corrected downstream gene.
biological_interpretation: The delta-GABA-A receptor perturbation is transcriptionally narrow and thalamus-centered; it does not trigger broad receptor-subunit or stress compensation and should mainly be followed as a Cttnbp2-positive thalamic marker response.

support.description: Gabrd has a strong thalamic self row plus a single Cttnbp2 non-target hit; Pvalb is target-engaged but buffered.

caveats: The Gabra4 signature-neighbor correlations to Gabrd/Gabrb2/Gabra1 were small, with unrelated Uba5 and Atp2b1 also near the top.
The dataset measures mRNA after partial knockdown, not tonic chloride current, receptor stoichiometry, gaboxadol sensitivity, or seizure behavior.
Cttnbp2 has no direct validated causal link to delta-GABA-A receptor physiology in this evidence.

prior_expectation.summary: GABRD is a delta subunit of extrasynaptic GABA-A chloride channels; delta-containing receptors mediate tonic inhibition in thalamic neurons and PV interneurons, but immediate receptor biology is expected to be electrophysiological rather than a broad mRNA program.

citations.citation: UniProtKB GABRD entries P22933 and O14764.
Cope et al., Journal of Neuroscience, 2005.
